item.title: Consumption trends of Cultural and Creative products in "phygital" contexts
item.content:encoded:
Elisa Salvador, ESSCA School of Management

Carmen Pérez-Cabañero, Universitat de Valencia

This special issue examines how consumption of cultural and creative products is evolving in contemporary "phygital" contexts where digital and physical experiences merge. The call seeks papers addressing contemporary theories of consumer behaviour, novel methodologies, and factors spanning economic, psychological, social, and technological dimensions that shape how people engage with cultural offerings.

The issue aims to map current consumption trends at individual and societal levels, identify best practices, and address gaps in academic understanding of how cultural industries are adapting to rapid societal transformation. It focuses on ten cultural domains including heritage, archives, libraries, publishing, visual arts, performing arts, audiovisual media, architecture, advertising, and crafts.

The special issue recognizes that cultural and creative industries are responding to challenges through innovation in digital environments, extended reality technologies, and sustainable practices. Papers should explore how these emerging practices contribute to individual wellbeing and broader social benefits such as education, intercultural dialogue, and social cohesion.

Appel publié par Arts and the Market. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Cultural and Creative Industries (CCIs) consumption patterns in phygital environments
  • Consumer behaviour theories and frameworks related to cultural products and services
  • Qualitative and quantitative methodologies for studying cultural consumption
  • Economic, psychological, social, and technological factors influencing purchasing decisions for cultural goods
  • Case studies of consumption trends across different geographic and cultural contexts
  • Phygital experiences integrating digital and physical elements in cultural settings
  • Role of artificial intelligence and extended reality technologies (augmented reality, virtual reality) in cultural consumption
  • Sustainability and circular practices in CCIs
  • Impact of CCIs on regional development, economic growth, cultural innovation, and social cohesion
  • Memorability and wellbeing benefits of phygital cultural experiences

Timeline

  • July 15, 2026: Opening date for manuscripts submissions
  • February 15, 2027: Closing date for manuscripts submission

item.title: Phygital Well-Being in Hybrid Tourism Destinations: Human-Centric Design, Management, and Visitor Welfare
item.content:encoded:
This special issue examines the intersection of physical and digital experiences in tourism destinations, focusing on how hybrid environments can be designed and managed to enhance visitor well-being. It seeks research addressing the implementation of human-centered design approaches that effectively blend tangible and virtual tourism elements while prioritizing the welfare of visitors and all stakeholders involved in the destination ecosystem.

Appel publié par Journal of Destination Marketing & Management. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Integration of physical and digital experiences in tourism destinations
  • Human-centric design principles for hybrid tourism environments
  • Management strategies for blended physical-digital tourism
  • Visitor welfare and well-being in phygital tourism contexts
  • Technology adoption and digital transformation in tourism
  • Experiential design combining tangible and virtual elements
  • Accessibility and inclusivity in hybrid tourism destinations
  • Emotional and psychological impacts of phygital experiences
  • Sustainable practices in digital-physical tourism integration
  • Stakeholder perspectives on hybrid tourism development

Timeline

  • July 30, 2028: Submission deadline
